content:
daphne: quick one — we're planning to change the analytics event shape to include a `route_priority` for routing-based quota accounting. thinking out loud about migration strategy.
sam: ah ok. current model uses `route_group` + heuristics for quota buckets right?
priya: yes. dashboards and alerting rely on route_group. adding route_priority lets routing choose cheaper model variants under quota pressure.
daphne: exactly. want to avoid breaking console cost dashboards and the per-route quota lookups. options: backfill + rename + index migration, or dual-write + read-side fallback.
lee: dual-write seems safest but expensive for disk + indexing. how big is the backfill surface? ~6 months of telemetry in hot tables? :thinking_face:
priya: hot table is ~700M rows for last 90d, backfill would be heavy but doable with chunked workers. main risk is long-running Tx/locks and increased RCU time.
daphne: another idea: keep route_group column, introduce a computed `route_priority` materialized view for new consumers, and gradually switch reads in console. Backfill only for dashboards needing historical continuity.
sam: can we avoid any table rewrite by computing `route_priority` in the query layer when `route_priority` is NULL? like COALESCE(route_priority, legacy_to_priority(route_group, attrs))
lee: yeah, but that means a function call in many analytics queries — could be heavy on big scans.
priya: we could push the conversion into the ingestion pipeline instead: streaming transform that emits both fields for new events and emits a patch job for recent days.
infra-bot: migration-checklist created: MIG-1937. Track shadow writes, backfill windows, index plan, SLA impact window.
daphne: draft SQL for a conservative backfill approach — chunked update by event_time + route_id:
```
-- example chunked backfill pseudo
BEGIN;
UPDATE analytics.events
SET route_priority = legacy_to_priority(route_group, metadata)
WHERE route_priority IS NULL
  AND event_time >= '2025-01-01' AND event_time < '2025-01-02'
  LIMIT 100000;
COMMIT;
```
we'd run per-day chunks with retries and a rate cap.
sam: ok. for indexes, add a nullable B-tree on (route_priority) then drop old index after everyone switched.
priya: dashboards: we should add compatibility layer in the console: new charts read `route_priority` if available, else compute from existing route_group. That avoids a hard cutover.
daphne: rollout UX: feature flag that flips console to prefer `route_priority` for 2 weeks per org, telemetry on mismatches.
lee: monitoring: add evals that compare quota decisions between legacy and new for a sample of traffic before full switch. record mismatch rate, cost delta.
priya: security/compliance: no PII change. KMS unaffected. Just audit logs of migration job.
daphne: timeline proposal: week 1 dual-write to new attr (ingest), week 2 run sampled backfill for last 7 days, week 3 full backfill for 90d, week 4 flip console flag org-by-org, week 6 drop route_group index and schedule vacuum.
sam: makes sense. any objections to materialized view approach instead of full backfill? pros: faster rollout; cons: slower query perf for large historical aggregates.
lee: if we go materialized view we still need periodic refreshs and to size space for it. I'm +1 for backfill if infra can handle the IO.
priya: I'll scope the backfill job and estimate CPU/IO. will post numbers by EOD.
daphne: thank you — I'll draft the migration playbook with the feature-flag gates and rollback steps. tag me for reviews.
sam: thanks. :thumbsup:
priya: tagging dashboards owners next: @dash-team please expect small data shape changes and a compatibility flag so charts keep working.
infra-bot: scheduled MIG-1937 dry-run on staging tomorrow 03:00 UTC — you'll get logs in #eng-platform-ops if anything fails.
daphne: cool. end-to-end plan looks solid. will update MIG doc with SQL snippets and index plan. :party-parrot:
